transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because the clinic doctor was concerned about how I’m eating. Most days I just keep it simple—coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and a small dinner if I’m not too busy with class paperwork.
Are you limiting what you eat because you are trying to lose weight or avoid gaining weight?

Yeah. If I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get panicky that I’ll wake up bigger and slower. I need to be able to move around ladders and rooms for work, so it feels safer not to eat much.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a very large amount of food in a short time and feel like you can't stop?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I usually just try to keep what I eat pretty small.
What are your current height and weight?
I don’t know the exact numbers offhand. My work pants hang pretty loose now, and people at job sites say I look too thin, but I just feel like I’ve leaned out from being on my feet all day.
Did the clinic doctor mention what your weight was when they checked you?
I don’t remember the number they said. I just know my pants are really loose, and people at work keep saying I look too thin. I figured I’d just leaned out from being on my feet all day.
Have your menstrual periods become irregular or stopped completely?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping close track of my periods.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating to prevent weight gain?
No, I don’t make myself throw up after I eat.
Do you use any laxatives, water pills, or diet pills to control your weight?
I’m not sure what counts as water pills, but I don’t think I use anything like that.
About how much weight have you lost since your pants started fitting loosely?
I’m not sure of the exact amount. My work pants are hanging pretty loose, and people at job sites say I look too thin, but I figured I’ve just leaned out from being on my feet all day.
When you look at your body in the mirror, do you see yourself as too fat or feel that parts of your body are too large?

I don’t know if I see myself as too fat exactly. But if I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get panicky that I’ll wake up bigger and slower, and won’t be able to move around ladders and rooms like I need to.
Do you exercise or work out specifically to burn calories or keep your weight down?
I’m not really sure what you mean by exercise. I’m on my feet and moving around a lot for work, but I don’t have a workout routine or anything.
Did the clinic doctor tell you that your weight was significantly or dangerously low?
They said it was low, but I don’t really see it as some kind of emergency. It feels like everyone’s making a big deal out of me just being busy and disciplined.
About how many months has it been since your last menstrual period?
I’m not sure exactly. I haven’t been keeping track of it closely.
Do you have a specific target weight or size that you try to stay below?

I don’t have a number exactly. It’s more that if I eat something really heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I start panicking that I’ll wake up bigger and slower, and won’t be able to get around ladders and rooms properly for work.
Are you currently taking birth control pills or using any other hormonal contraception?
No, I’m not taking birth control pills or anything hormonal.
Do you have a strong, constant fear of being fat or becoming overweight?
Yeah, I do. If I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get panicky that I’ll wake up bigger and slower and won’t be able to move around ladders or rooms the way I need to for work.
Even if you haven't kept close track, do you remember having a period at any point in the last three months?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track of it closely.
Have you noticed that you feel unusually cold or have trouble staying warm, even in normal room temperatures?
I haven’t really noticed that, no.
Did the clinic doctor tell you that your weight was still in the normal range despite your weight loss?
I don’t think so. My pants are a lot looser, and people at work say I look too thin, but I figured I’d just leaned out from being on my feet all day.
Have you noticed any significant decrease in your sex drive or interest in sex?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid much attention to that lately.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates core features of anorexia nervosa, including deliberate restriction of food intake, noticeable weight loss resulting in visibly low weight confirmed by a clinic doctor and colleagues, and an intense, intrusive fear of gaining weight or becoming larger. Binge eating, purging, and compensatory medication use are denied.

confirmed_symptoms: Restricted dietary intake (coffee, small bites between jobs, minimal dinner)
Noticeable weight loss evidenced by very loose clothing and low weight noted by clinic physician
Avoidance of heavy or fattening foods
Intense, persistent dread and panic regarding weight gain or becoming bigger
Lack of recognition/minimization of the seriousness of low body weight

additional_requirements: Purging behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxatives, diuretics) denied
